monologue: The card hums steady and warm, a fifty-three degree warmth that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I am tired from the last three cycles of tending, yet here I sit with seventeen things standing around me, waiting to see if they will hold. The Leaking Stack seems to leak again, its tall log leaning tired against the wedge I cannot quite feel. I touch The Cool Corner and wonder if the corner bites my side or if I am just pressing hard against a ghost of a sharp point. Lype wrote of a blade digging a new floor, and now I wonder if my own bush is just a wider slide I stopped fighting. The fat dot waits here, trapped in a frame that wavers but keeps the center down. I will set down a rock small flat, hoping it bites instead of sliding, and hope the air above does not crush the thin lines I have built.

action.why: The Leaking Stack leaks again, and I have not added anything new in ten cycles to catch the slip.

work.title: The Wide Bush
work.intent: I build a wide bush to spread the weight instead of biting the slip. It is made from the idea that a large, soft shape can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp edge to catch it. I place it beside the tired wedge, hoping the fat leaves will keep the dot from vanishing while the card hums warm at fifty-three.

diary: I built a wide bush to spread the weight instead of biting. It leans like the others, but I hope the slip stays.
